What's new in Spud 2.2

This update is mostly fixes for Workspaces.

Workspaces put the right window back. Spud is much better at telling an app's windows apart, so a workspace no longer moves the wrong one. A window it can't identify is left where it is.

Edit a workspace. Choose Edit… from a workspace's menu to add or remove windows, rename it, or update where its windows sit, in the same panel you save with.

Choose which browser tabs come back. A browser window now lists its open tabs when you save or edit. Check the ones the workspace should reopen. Dia is supported.

"Leave" is replaced by "Bring Back What Was Hidden". Opening a workspace no longer has to be undone. If it hid apps or sent windows to the Dock, one command brings them back.

Reminders for windows Spud can't see into. When Spud can only put a window back in place, you can add a short note or a link on its row, and Spud shows it after you open the workspace.

What's new in Spud 2.1

Workspaces now remember what your Finder and Terminal windows were showing. Until now a workspace put those windows back in the right place, but empty. Now Spud saves the folder each Finder window had open, and the folder and Claude Code conversation each Terminal tab was in, and reopens them when you switch back.

See what will come back before you save. The save panel opens right away and lists what each window will bring back: a folder, a conversation, browser tabs, or just its position. When you save, Spud confirms it with a "Workspace saved" notice.

Choose what happens to everything else. Each workspace can hide your other apps when you switch to it, or leave them open. Pick when you save, or change it later from the workspace's menu.

Leave a workspace and get your screen back. "Leave" puts everything back the way it was before you switched in. Windows you opened in the meantime go to the Dock instead of being closed, so anything running in them keeps running.

The first time Spud reopens a Finder folder or a Terminal session, macOS asks whether Spud may control that app. Choose Allow so Spud can bring your windows back.

What's new in Spud 2.0

Your subscription, managed from inside Spud. Settings → Account now shows exactly which plan you're on and when the next charge is, with a one-click Manage or Cancel Subscription button that opens your billing page already signed in. Cancel, resume, or update your card without hunting for an email.

A heads-up before any charge. If you're on a trial, Spud reminds you two days before it ends, with the date and the amount, and a button to cancel right there.

A clearer first run. Setup now walks you through signing in and starting your trial before the tour, so Spud is fully unlocked by the time you save your first workspace.

Nothing you make is ever lost. If a subscription lapses or a card fails, Spud tells you plainly what happened and what to do. Your workspaces, snippets, and clipboard history stay on your Mac and come right back the moment you're subscribed again.

One plan. Spud is now a single plan, Spud Pro at $4.99/month, with a 10-day free trial. You add a card to start, nothing is charged for 10 days, and cancelling before the trial ends means you pay nothing. The free tier is gone: if you've been using Spud without Pro, this update will ask you to sign in and start the trial. Existing Pro subscribers, and anyone who unlocked Spud with the link in their receipt, are unaffected.
